rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This problem-solving plan begins with the meaning and procedure of the product rule, then moves to guided use and independent practice. It assumes the power rule is familiar but briefly verifies it. Four short sessions fit the available 15-minute windows, keep one action prominent at a time, and include a complete example before a similar attempt.

sessions.title: Why the Product Rule Is Needed
sessions.objective: Understand when and why the product rule applies.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule concept and one worked derivative
contentTargets: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions
Connect the product rule formula to its two derivative terms
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor and multiplying the results is incorrect
Apply the product rule to one problem that uses simple power-rule derivatives

sessions.title: Follow the Product Rule Procedure
sessions.objective: Use a reliable sequence to differentiate a product.
sessions.amountLabel: One procedure and one guided application
contentTargets: Identify the two factors and their derivatives
Substitute correctly into (fg)' = f'g + fg'
completionEvidence: Construct a correctly labeled product-rule setup
Solve one similar derivative with step-by-step guidance

sessions.title: Handle Algebra and Function Variations
sessions.objective: Apply the rule when factors require simplification or different derivative rules.
contentTargets: Differentiate products involving constants and polynomial factors
Simplify the resulting derivative without losing a term
completionEvidence: Solve one polynomial product derivative without a provided setup
Compare the result before and after algebraic simplification

sessions.title: Independent Product Rule Check
sessions.objective: Choose and apply the product rule independently, then repair any error.
sessions.amountLabel: Three short mixed derivative decisions and applications
contentTargets: Decide whether a derivative requires the product rule
Apply the complete rule independently
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by whether they require the product rule
Solve two product-rule derivatives independently and explain each term

activities.body: State when an expression counts as a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions

activities.feedback: A complete answer names two separate differentiable factors and the multiplication between them.

activities.label: Fix the missing idea
activities.title: Repair the recognition

activities.feedback: Repair the gap by naming both factors and the multiplication between them. If there is not a product of two functions, the product rule is not the match.

activities.body: Give the idea again in one or two sentences.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions

activities.feedback: A strong response is brief, accurate, and clearly names the two-factor product structure.

activities.body: Choose the expression that is a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions
activities.feedback: The correct choice multiplies two differentiable functions. The others are a sum or a single function.

check.referenceAnswer: When it is written as two factors and both factors are differentiable at the point of interest.
check.feedback: The key condition is differentiability of both factors at the same point.

recognitionCheck.title: Spot the product form
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which expression is a product of two differentiable functions?
recognitionCheck.feedback: Only the first choice is a direct product of two factors.
